DAAS Assistant
Say what you want to make — an email to a group, a new event or form, or a list of people. The right builder opens prefilled; nothing sends or saves until you confirm there. (Questions go to Research Chat.)
Quick Capture

Dump anything — a pasted email, a quick thought, a PDF or screenshot of a conversation, or a voice note. It'll figure out which contact it belongs to and propose what to log. Nothing saves until you confirm.

Build Profiles
Search modes explained

All three answer questions about your people. The difference is how much information they look at before answering — which affects speed, depth, and cost.

Quick · ~10k tokens · cheapest, fastest

Skims a one-line summary of every household — name, family members, prospect score, home value, and total giving. It does not read your notes or interactions. Best for fast roster questions like "who are my top-scoring families in Newton?" Answers in a single paragraph.

Standard · ~35k tokens · the everyday default

Everything Quick sees, plus it searches your notes and interactions for the ones most relevant to your question and reads those too. Best for most real questions — "who mentioned wanting to host a Shabbat dinner?" — where the answer lives in your notes. Needs embeddings generated to find notes.

Power Search · ~80–100k tokens · slow & costly (~$0.30)

The deepest look. Reads the full detailed profile of every household — prospect-score breakdown, gift history, AI research summary, suggested approach, business info — plus the relevant notes. Use for big cross-database thinking like "build me a major-gift prospect list with talking points for each." Asks you to confirm before running because of the cost.

"Tokens" is roughly how much text the AI reads per question. More tokens = more thorough but slower and more expensive. When unsure, start with Standard.
